messages.author: 48f24841e806e6c6
messages.subject: The R Statistical JSON server
parts:
So to stimulate some discussion, is anyone interested in doing this?
The idea is really simple:

1: Provide a Rook applications that executes a given R function and
returns the result in JSON format.

2. The url will look something like http://example.com/srv/rnorm or
http://example.com/srv/base::rnorm.

3. Input can be CGI GET or POST variables when sensible. For instance
http://example.com/srv/rnorm?n=1&mean=100&sd=.5

4. Input can be as a JSON object via POST payload.

5. Output is a JSON object.

I've spoken with various individuals who are or have worked on
something like this, and I think it really needs to be standardized.
Also, which package is better for implementing this: RJSONIO or rjson.

Jeff

messages.author: 42eed4e1caba0ad0
messages.subject: Re: The R Statistical JSON server
parts:
Well, I always do that "by hand"... i.e. when I was building a RApache
app, I used to save results as a list, then serialized them with
toJSON. Of course, you can serialize pretty much anything with JSON.
About form serialization, I use jQuery's .serialize() method. You just
need appropriate form selector, and you're good to go: $
("form").serialize()
The function returns a string in "n=1&mean=100&sd=.5" format (like in
GET request).

I'm not sure if I could carry out such a project from scratch, but if
you're looking for a guinea pig/collaborator/alpha|beta-tester/etc.
I'm in! =) Anyway, did you provide "rnorm" deliberately, or as a
meaningful "foobar" replacement? I hope that you have something
specific in mind (and I should definitely port my RApache app to Rook,
I'm being lazy as hell!!!)

Oh, and, I vote for RJSONIO, since it's faster. At least they say so
on package page:

This is an alternative to rjson package. That version is too slow for
converting large R objects to JSON and is not extensible, but a very
useful prototype. It is fast for parsing. This package uses methods,
vectorized operations and C code and callbacks to R functions for
deserializing JSON objects to R. Verison 0.4 of this package uses a
new native parser, implements the transformation code in C and
allocates memory efficiently (rather than concatenating because of
event driven parsing). The result is a significantly faster parsing of
large JSON documents.

messages.subject: Re: The R Statistical JSON server
parts:
Using a json api as a web service is a general method that is used in many, many applications. I don't think anyone holds exclusive rights to do this. I have been using json R web services long before revolution had their product (as shown on my useR 2009 slides), so I cannot imagine that they suddenly consider this as infringement.

Also note that 'copyright' only applies to actual source code. You cannot hold copyright to a method or technique.

This is on github as well, but posting here to discuss:

# https://github.com/jeffreyhorner/rRack/blob/master/Rook/inst/exampleApps/RJSONIO.R

library(RJSONIO)
app <- function(env){
req <- Request$new(env)
res <- Response$new()

obj <- sub('^/','',req$path_info())


# Get out of here fast if no object exists
if (!exists(obj)) return(res$finish())

# res$write(paste(capture.output(str(req
$params()),file=NULL),collapse='\n'))
# return(res$finish())

# Gather args from one of three sources: GET, POST as a x-www-
urlencoded,
# or POST as JSON payload. params() squishes GET and POST together
when
# POST is x-www-urlencoded.
if (!is.null(req$params())) {
args <- req$params()
} else {
# TODO: Collect POST payload and pass to RJSONIO
args <- list()
}

# Normalize arguments to R types if necessary. Integers to
integer, Numerics to numeric, etc.
# Maybe we can propose a vector syntax in CGI that's coherent,
too.
for (i in names(args)){

# Keep as character anything that starts with a quote char
if (grepl('^[\'"]',args[[i]]))
next

# Integer
if (grepl('^[+-]?\\d+$',args[[i]]))
args[[i]] <- as.integer(args[[i]])

# Numeric. need to add scientific notation
if (grepl('^[+-]?[0-9.]+$',args[[i]]))
args[[i]] <- as.numeric(args[[i]])
}

if (is.function(get(obj)))
res$write(toJSON(do.call(obj,args)))
else
res$write(toJSON(get(obj)))

res$finish()

}
